rationale: Both candidates converge on the same real, high-value gap the human reviewers (who only said LGTM) missed: two reliability test files (test_invalid_image_generation.py, test_invalid_image_editing.py) still encode the old layers=3 boundary and old error-message substrings, which will now fail. Both also correctly validate the core 4-file diff is internally consistent. Y presents the finding more cleanly with exact before/after code snippets and crisper 'update to X' actions, and its secondary note about confirming the H100 layers=2 run is appropriately hedged as non-blocking; X's parallel finding on this point leans on an unverifiable 'gate_report FAILURE' claim and adds a scope-creep suggestion (add a new positive test) that isn't really a defect. Recall is capped for both since ground truth contains essentially no substantive concerns to recall against.
